findings.finding: Reviewer close of the author's open finding: claim() waits for the submit commit. submit takes lockAttempt (jobs.ts:200) before dispatch (jobs.ts:259), and pg_advisory_xact_lock holds until COMMIT (database.ts:29), so the workflow cannot exist before the lock is held. claim() takes the same lock first (jobs.ts:287). Its next statement, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (jobs.ts:288), runs under READ COMMITTED: database.ts:23 issues a bare BEGIN and nothing in packages, shared or tools sets an isolation level, so that statement takes a fresh snapshot after the lock is granted and sees the committed row. If submit rolls back after dispatch, claim reads no row and throws 404, and the run fails without paid work, the same end state as the old wait step after its retries.
findings.none: Sound by walkthrough. A two-connection Postgres test stays a follow-up because PGlite has one connection.

findings.finding: No lock cycle and no pool starvation. Every path that takes the attempt advisory lock (submit, claim, requestCancellation) takes it before any row lock on that attempt. update, heartbeat, markProviderStarted, acknowledge and reconcile take only the row lock. A claim waiting on the lock waits on a submit that already holds its own pooled connection, so the max-4 pool cannot deadlock.
findings.none: Walked every lockAttempt and lockStateWithoutCheckpoint caller in jobs.ts.

findings.finding: Crash and retry stay convergent with one step. Workflow re-runs a step with the same stepId (node_modules/workflow/docs/foundations/idempotency.mdx: stable across retries), and claimId is that stepId, so a re-run or a second dispatch finds job.claimId set and claim() returns false. reconcile marks a stale reply interrupted once. The worker.test.ts crash test covers the convergence.

If a chunk write's COMMIT succeeds but the client sees an error (connection lost after COMMIT), the writer puts the batch back and the failed or interrupted write appends it again, so that text and its provider events appear twice. The old code lost the text in the same case instead. Rare, and the terminal write on a dead connection usually fails too.
findings.none: Minor, not blocking. Accepting duplication over loss on an ambiguous commit is a reasonable trade.
